remarks_1999: Double entries Downtown Gallery Archive. Whitney Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks indicate, "Exam. at Whitney Museum, April 1946.... On backing: By O'Keeffe 'Series I – 1919 – The Plains'/Georgia O'Keeffe. Star initials." Whitney Archive indicates, "Note: he above title [From the Plains] give by O'Keeffe." Pictured in 1923 New York (Anderson) Stieglitz installation photograph, see Appendix III, figure 15. O'Keeffe wrote: "*From the Plains* was painted from something I heard very often – a very special rhythm that would go on for hours and hours – that was shy I painted it again a couple of years ago – From experiences of one kind or another shapes and colors come to me very clearly" (Georgia O'Keeffe to John I. H. Baur, 22 April 1947,Whitney Archive). Mentioned in 1934 *New York Times* (1934). Titled *A Song* by O'Keeffe on Abiquiú Notebooks photograph. (Source: Lynes, 1999)

description: Vertical canvas with cloudy blue, green, and cream colored formation filling the bottom half of the painting.  Hovering over this in a black background is a foggy streak of red.  The upper half of the canvas is traversed by a lightening bolt zig-zag shape in greenish white that cuts through the blue-black of the background.
